provenance: All values are literature-derived engineering estimates for decision-support software, NOT measured reliability. Named sources are listed in data/SOURCES.md; codes R03, R06-R11 and R17-R36 refer to a research dossier not included in this repository (several read at abstract level only - see gaps), and bands resting on them should be read as published starting points.

units.yield_strength: MPa (tensile stress at yield; for rPET values are strength at break where single number reported)
units.elongation: % (elongation at break for printed parts unless noted)

two_level_model.description: lot mean multiplier m ~ LogNormal(1, cv_lot); within-lot specimen multiplier s ~ LogNormal(1, cv_within); property value = nominal_mean * m * s; cv_total^2 = cv_lot^2 + cv_within^2 (approximately, for small CVs). Correlations applied between log-properties via a Gaussian copula with the given correlation matrix.
two_level_model.default_split_rationale: Within-sample specimen SDs reported by Eriksen et al. are <=1-4% of the mean for PE/PP strength, while between-sample/source spreads are 20-50% (R04). PNAS measured 17.7% across 10 plates from one supplier (R01), versus 54% across the literature (R01). This is consistent with lot-to-lot variance dominating for E and yield strength; hence sqrt(0.85)=0.92 of the total CV is assigned to lots and 0.39 to within-lot scatter. For elongation/impact, specimen scatter is much larger (PP impact SD 12-15 on 19-33 kJ/m2, R04; rPP elongation 10-100% across lots, R05), so a 0.60 lot variance fraction is used.
two_level_model.previous_v0_1_split: cv_lot = 0.8*cv_total, cv_within = 0.6*cv_total implies 64%/36% variance split - this dossier recommends 85/15 (E, sigma_y) and 60/40 (elongation) unless the user supplies lot data.
two_level_model.warning: The split is an evidenced inference, not a direct measurement of a single population. 'ASSUMPTION' is recorded per-property in lot_vs_within.

correlations.basis: ASSUMPTION. No verified source in this dossier reports a correlation coefficient between modulus and yield strength across recyclate lots. Polymer physics supports positive E-sigma_y and negative E-elongation coupling. Keep as user-visible sensitivity parameters; the PNAS UATSC model also treated modulus and interface strength as independent (R01).

rpet.name: Recycled polyethylene terephthalate (bottle-grade rPET, flakes/regranulate; injection moulding, extrusion, or filament extrusion)

lnE_lnYieldStrength.note: No recyclate-specific correlation coefficient recovered in any verified source; value consistent with polymer-physics expectation and PNAS's independent-treatment choice [R01]. Treat as a sensitivity parameter.

rpet.notes: rPET is the recyclate with the strongest 'IV can be restored by SSP' evidence [R22], so quality is highly process-dependent: an SSP-equipped supplier is a different feedstock class from a simple re-pelletiser. Software should expose a 'process route' switch rather than one rPET preset.

E.evidence: rPET flexural modulus from 20 commercial recyclates >=1860 MPa and generally below vPET literature (ISO 178) [R08]; literature-compiled rPET modulus range broadly 1800-3500 MPa [R01 Fig.1A]; no single multi-supplier tensile-modulus dataset recovered.

yield_strength.evidence: Lab-reprocessed, undried rPET shows 22.1-36.3 MPa at break (explicitly not industrial-scale) [R04]; bottle-grade rPET spec-range is 50-60+ MPa but no multi-supplier measurement recovered -> mean lowered conservatively; GRADE C / partially assumption.

elongation.evidence: rPET strain at break 2.1-3.4% (lab) [R04]; elongation at flexural strength 4.8-5.2% (20 commercial recyclates) [R08].

density.evidence: Typical semi-crystalline bottle-grade PET density 1.33-1.37; not measured in the extracted sources -> ASSUMPTION (low CV justified by density being a contractual spec that recyclers control).

rpetg.name: Recycled PETG (glycol-modified PET, filament/printed or extruded sheet regrind)

lnE_lnYieldStrength.note: Not measured; printed PETG within-batch CV is small (R07) so correlation has second-order effect.

rpetg.notes: The four rPETG sources agree that mechanical knockdown after 1-6 reprocessing cycles is small (single-digit % to ~10%), unlike rPET. For a printed-part product the dominant scatter may be printing/porosity rather than polymer batch - AnyRB's feedstock model should be calibrated with printed-coupon data, not just filament data.

E.evidence: Printed ISO 527-2 specimens: new filament 2.28 GPa (SD 0.25, CV 10.8%), recycled-once 2.17 GPa (SD 0.18, CV 8.3%), n=6 each [R07]; vendor spec 2-3 GPa.

yield_strength.evidence: Peak tensile stress 46.5 MPa (SD 0.66) new vs 48.6 MPa (SD 1.54) recycled-once, ISO 527-2, n=6 [R07]; vendor tensile 50-70 MPa. Use printed-part values for printed lattice.

elongation.evidence: Strain at peak stress 3.15-3.51% for printed PETG [R07]. NB: bulk rPETG elongation is tens of percent - printed-part brittleness is a process effect; software should model the printed part, so the low value is deliberate.

density.evidence: Vendor spec 1.23 g/cm3 [R07]; common PETG datasheets 1.23-1.27 -> ASSUMPTION on CV.

rhdpe.name: Recycled high-density polyethylene (PCR rigid bottles/containers from MRFs)

lnE_lnYieldStrength.note: Not measured for recyclates; PNAS modelled E and interface strength independently [R01]. Sensitivity parameter.

lnE_elongation.note: Direction motivated by degradation evidence (stiffer/embrittled after oxidation [R19]) but no coefficient measured.

rhdpe.notes: Strongest-evidenced preset. Two useful sub-cases: (a) 'film-grade rHDPE' E ~1,350 MPa CV 0.18; (b) 'MRF-mixed rigid rHDPE' E ~700-900 MPa CV 0.25-0.30. If only one preset is allowed, keep this compromise and let the user shift the mean.

E.evidence: Across three US MRFs rHDPE modulus spans 380-1,250 MPa [R02 via R01]; one industrial stretch-film stream measured 1,350 +/- 239 MPa (CV 17.7%, n=50/10 plates) [R01]; literature-compiled n=40 mean 1,213 +/- 654 MPa (CV 54%, includes method heterogeneity) [R01]. Recommended preset sits between MRF-mixed and film-grade; treat as GRADE B.

yield_strength.evidence: HDPE-rich reprocessed samples 41.6-48.4 MPa; externally sourced mixed PE 22.2-38.3 MPa [R04]. Bimodality (pure rHDPE vs mixed PE) is the dominant lot-level effect; preset = mid-range mixed PCR-HDPE.

elongation.evidence: Strain at yield 11.2-15.2% (HDPE-rich) and 13.3-17.0% (mixed PE) [R04]; ductile 'no break' behaviour. Elongation at break after degradation can be much lower (embrittlement under thermo-oxidative reprocessing [R19]) -> wide CV, GRADE B/C.

density.evidence: Virgin HDPE control 0.946 g/cm3 [R12]; rHDPE is sorted by density and sold against a density spec -> low CV is an engineering assumption.

rpp.name: Recycled polypropylene (PCR rigid packaging/household PP)

lnE_lnYieldStrength.note: Filler content drives both E and density but not necessarily yield strength; no measured coefficient.

lnE_elongation.note: Filler content increases E and strongly reduces elongation at break [R05]; direction well motivated, coefficient not measured.

rpp.notes: Hinczica et al. [R05] is the most direct batch-to-batch evidence in the whole library: all 10 lots met the same MFR and density specification, yet elongation at break ranged 10-100% and fatigue life ranged 3000-6.52e6 cycles. MFR/density specs are NOT sufficient acceptance criteria. Filler content (2-24 wt%) should be a first-class lot parameter.

E.evidence: Across MRFs, rPP modulus ~650 MPa in one MRF vs roughly double in the other two [R02]; process-sorted IM rPP 434-472 MPa under a different test protocol [R03]; PP is usually the stiffest common PCR polyolefin in practice. Large protocol discrepancy -> GRADE B, do not over-trust absolute value.

yield_strength.evidence: Reprocessed PP tensile strength at yield 24.9-28.7 MPa across 11 samples [R04]; process-sorted IM rPP yield 12.1-13.3 MPa (protocol-dependent) [R03]. Spec MFR/density compliant lots still vary in filler (2-24 wt%) [R05].

elongation.evidence: Elongation at break of 10 PCR-PP lots over 15 months: 10-100% [R05]; strain at yield 6.6-11.9% [R04]. High CV is the headline finding for rPP.

density.evidence: Virgin PP control 0.900 g/cm3 [R12]; filled PCR-PP sold to 0.97 +/- 0.03 g/cm3 spec with 2-24 wt% filler [R05] -> real rPP density is a filler-content proxy and should be shifted with filler %.

rldpe.name: Recycled low-density polyethylene (PCR film/flexible
rldpe.notes: Weakest-evidenced preset; included because LDPE is part of mixed PE streams and is the usual cause of low-strength PE recyclate [R04]. Do not use for structural claims.

E.evidence: Literature-compiled recycled-PE modulus ranges (approximate reading of R01 Fig.1A): rLDPE roughly 150-350 MPa, far below rHDPE; no rLDPE-specific multi-supplier dataset recovered.

yield_strength.evidence: Typical LDPE tensile strength ~10 MPa cited by R04; rLDPE from post-consumer waste showed 'satisfactory' static/cyclic performance in R33 without tabulated values.

elongation.evidence: Typical LDPE ductility is very high; rLDPE retains ductility in R33. Mostly ASSUMPTION.

mixed_polyolefins.name: Mixed polyolefins (e.g. #3-7 bale / commingled PE-PP)
mixed_polyolefins.notes: For mixed streams, composition (wt% PP, filler, PET/PS contamination) is a better lot descriptor than any single mechanical property - see proxy models.

E.evidence: Mixed plastic waste from MRFs shows large modulus variability across MRFs, largest for HDPE (380-1,250 MPa) [R02 via R01]; #3-7 bales contained PP up to 79 wt% [R02]. Preset is a blend assumption, GRADE D.

yield_strength.evidence: Assumption built from rHDPE/rPP ranges [R04]; PE-PP immiscibility degrades properties [R12].

elongation.evidence: Assumption; PP-rich vs PE-rich composition changes failure mode drastically (10-100% for rPP alone [R05]).

density.evidence: Density of PE/PP mixture 0.90-0.96 depending on PP fraction; ASSUMPTION.

proxy_models.input: melt viscosity / MFR measured during compounding or in-mould (cheap, per lot; supplier datasheet or inline sensor)
proxy_models.target: tensile strength and Charpy impact of the lot
proxy_models.relation: Quantile/regression map from viscosity to strength/impact, calibrated per supplier: q_hat = a + b*ln(eta/eta_ref) with b>0 for strength and impact up to the point of over-degradation; a random-forest/RNN classifier can classify lots into property bins. NO closed-form universal relation was found.
proxy_models.accuracy: Classification of 23 household rPP lots achieved >85% accuracy (R06). Closed-loop in-mould rheology control held mechanical-property and weight CV <5% on 5 rPP blends (R14). CAVEAT: MFR alone is demonstrably insufficient for rPP (R02 notes MFR did not track mechanical properties; Jmal et al. 2018 in R02).
proxy_models.status: usable as classification/first-order proxy, must carry residual uncertainty >=15-20%; label 'proxy, calibrate with own lot data'
proxy_models.residual_uncertainty_cv: 0.15-0.25 (assumption from classifier accuracy and caution in R02/R06)

proxy_models.input: NIR / NIR-assisted flake analysis of feedstock composition (polymer mix, filler/ash proxies) or hyperspectral sorting signal
proxy_models.target: density, crystallinity, short-chain branching, impact resistance
proxy_models.relation: PLS/ML regression on spectra; composition (wt% other polymers) strongly correlates with impact resistance.
proxy_models.accuracy: NIR-assisted flake analysis was the best composition method and strongly correlated with rPE impact resistance (R36); adding 'other PE types' reduced impact resistance by 11% at the first step (R36). PLS predicts polyolefin density/crystallinity/SCB from NIR with high accuracy (R31), but R2/RMSE values were not extractable in this study - do not quote an accuracy number.
proxy_models.status: usable for lot fingerprints / acceptance rules, not yet a calibrated property predictor in this dossier

proxy_models.relation: IV is monotonically linked to molecular weight and mechanical performance in principle; SSP can restore IV (R22).
proxy_models.accuracy: No quantitative IV-to-mechanical-property mapping was recovered from verified sources -> NOT provided.
proxy_models.status: gap - do not implement a numeric IV predictor yet

gaps: No verified recyclate-specific correlation coefficient between E and yield strength (or E and elongation) was found; all correlations in this library are marked assumption.

Within-lot vs lot-to-lot variance decomposition is inferred from specimen SDs reported in R04 and cross-study spreads in R01, not measured with a nested design. The split factors (0.85/0.60) remain assumptions.

rPET tensile modulus and yield strength: only flexural/impact data from 20 commercial recyclates (R08) and lab-scale undried PET tensile data (R04) were recoverable; rPET yield strength (45 MPa) is deliberately conservative.
rPETG full text (R07) is one recycling cycle; long-run rPETG degradation numbers are qualitative only (R09-R11).
Full texts of R05 (Wiley), R06 (ACS), R14 (Wiley), R22 (MDPI), R31 (ACS) were paywalled/blocked for automated access; their numbers come from abstracts only.
Cecon et al. 2023 per-MRF Young's modulus values are reported in figures; the 380-1,250 MPa range is verified via the PNAS quotation (R01) but not re-extracted from the primary figure.
No verified data on the *seasonality* of rHDPE composition (only rPP over 15 months, R05).
_corrections_to_spec: PNAS 2025 e2502613122 authors are Georgiou, Sun, Liu, Athanasiou - PRODUCT_SPEC.md says 'Ghosh et al.'; correct the attribution.
J. Appl. Polym. Sci. 10.1002/app.70501 is published 2026 (issue 15), not 2025; use year 2026.
The PRODUCT_SPEC 'CV(E)=0.20' for rHDPE is defensible as a total CV; the recommended value is 0.22 with a documented sub-case split (film-grade 0.18 vs MRF-mixed 0.25-0.30).
The v0.1 two-level split CV_lot=0.8*CV_total / CV_within=0.6*CV_total (64/36 variance) over-weights within-lot scatter for E and yield strength; evidence supports ~85/15 for those properties.
